newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek 97 avg CPI inflation seen at 7.0pct - EIU.
newsitem.headline: Greek 97 avg CPI inflation seen at 7.0pct - EIU.

text.p: Greek consumer inflation should fall to 7.0 percent in 1997 from 8.5 percent in 1996 but the viability of the downward trend depends on productivity gains, the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said.
"There have been hopeful signs with reduced consumer and wholesale price rises in the second half of 1996," said the EIU in its quarterly report on the Greek economy.
"With wages expected to increase by a little more than prices, however, the maintenance of a sustainable downward trend in 1997 and 1998 will depend on productivity gains," it added.

The hard drachma policy which contained imported energy, raw material and intermediate good prices, making up two-thirds of all inputs to local manufacturers, was the major weapon against inflation, it said.
The EIU warned that market confidence could evaporate if economic fundamentals, namely the current account deficit, worsened.
This could tempt borrowers to unwind their short-term forex positions leading to a depletion of central bank reserves.
However, the report said the hard drachma policy would not deter a pick up in 1997 export growth on the back of strong investment projects and a business expansion drive in the Balkans and elsewhere.
The current account deficit will widen from an estimated $4.0 billion in 1996 -- 3.5 percent of GDP -- to $4.5 billion in 1997 or 3.6 percent of GDP.
The general government budget deficit will drop to 5.0 percent of GDP from 7.6 percent in 1996, predicted the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU).
